record.original_question: (E. Zelmanov). Let F be a field of characteristic p > 0, and let Γ be the principal congruence subgroup of Aut(F [x1,..., xn ]) consisting of all automorphisms that send each variable xi to xi modulo terms of higher degree. Then Γ is a residuallyp group. Does Γ satisfy a pro-p identity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $F[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be the polynomial ring in $n$ variables over $F$. Let $\mathrm{Aut}(F[x_1,\dots,x_n])$ denote the group of $F$-algebra automorphisms of $F[x_1,\dots,x_n]$. Define the principal congruence subgroup
$$\Gamma = \{\,\varphi \in \mathrm{Aut}(F[x_1,\dots,x_n]) : \varphi(x_i) \equiv x_i \pmod{\mathfrak{m}^2}\ \text{for each } i=1,\dots,n\,\},$$
where $\mathfrak{m} = (x_1,\dots,x_n)$, i.e., $\Gamma$ consists of those automorphisms sending each variable $x_i$ to $x_i$ plus terms of degree $\ge 2$. It is known that $\Gamma$ is a residually-$p$ group, so it has a pro-$p$ completion $\widehat{\Gamma}_p$.

A pro-$p$ group $G$ is said to satisfy a pro-$p$ identity if there exists a non-identity element $w$ in the free pro-$p$ group $\widehat{F}_d$ on some finite set of generators such that every continuous homomorphism $\widehat{F}_d \to G$ sends $w$ to the identity.

Question: Does $\Gamma$ (equivalently, its pro-$p$ completion) satisfy a pro-$p$ identity?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was posed by E. Zelmanov as a new entry in the 2026 problem-collection of group theory problems. Related work (e.g., on pro-p identities in linear groups by Zelmanov and others) has shown pro-p identities for GL_n over pro-finite rings under conditions on p, but no published result resolves the specific question for the principal congruence subgroup of Aut(F[x_1,...,x_n]). No source was found settling this question, so it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Pro-p identities of linear groups
status_evidence.snippet: In 2005, inspired by the solution of the Specht problem, Zelmanov sketched a proof for the following generalization: if n is a natural number, then for every p >> n, GL_n(R) satisfies a pro-p identity.
status_evidence.claim: Background context: Zelmanov-style pro-p identity results are known for linear groups but not specifically for Aut(F[x_1,...,x_n]).

status_evidence.title: Lie algebras and torsion groups with identity (arXiv:1604.05678)
status_evidence.snippet: Related work on identities in pro-p groups and Lie algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Surrounding literature on pro-p identities, none resolving Zelmanov's question for the polynomial-ring automorphism congruence subgroup.
